title: AI Can Be a Great Math Tutor—If You Use It the Right Way
summary:
Imagine having a tutor that never gets tired and can explain math in a million different ways. That's what AI can be! But a new survey of 1,300 top high school math students from the U.S., England, and Wales found that AI is only helpful if you use it the right way.

The students, who all took part in a big math contest, said AI is great for explaining things step by step, checking homework, and answering "why" questions. It can even help you feel less nervous about math. More than 200 math teachers agreed—six out of ten said AI could be a good tutor.

But there's a catch. Robbie Torney from Common Sense Media says learning needs "friction"—that means it should feel a little hard. If AI just gives you the answer, you don't learn. "You have to work through things that feel hard and come up with your own answers," he says.

Tiago, a high school senior from Colorado, agrees. "I won't use AI before I've fully attempted a problem," he says. Most students in the survey (63 percent) said they always try a problem on their own first. If they're stuck, they ask their teacher (58 percent) or classmates (50 percent) before turning to AI (39 percent).

Teachers worry that AI can become a crutch—something you lean on too much. Amanda Brown, a math teacher, says she sees kids with perfect homework scores who later fail tests because they used AI to do the work. "You're gonna have to take the test without AI," she reminds us.

So what's the trick? Use AI in moderation. Ask specific questions like, "What are different ways I could solve this?" and always add, "Don't give me the answer." That way, AI helps you learn instead of doing the learning for you.
why_it_matters: Learning to use AI wisely now can help you build real problem-solving skills, which are useful in school and in future jobs.
